newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh plans to make taka fully convertible.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh plans to make taka fully convertible.

text.p: The Governor of Bangladesh Bank, the central bank, Lutfar Rahman Sarker, said on Saturday the government would complete the process of making the taka fully convertible in the new fiscal year beginning in July.
"We have started a process to make the taka convertible on capital account from the next fiscal year," Sarkar told a meeting of the Economic Reporters' Forum.
Sarker did not explain the process but said: "The government will apply the knowledge and expertise gathered in course of implementing the convertibility of the taka on current (trade) account."
"But to accomplish this job there must be stability on both political and economic fronts at home and abroad."
Bangladesh made the taka convertible on the current account in 1994.
Sarker said the government would need foreign exchange reserves of at least $2.3 billion to enable it to make the taka fully convertible. Bangladesh now has $1.86 billion in reserves.

Sarker said the taka was "strong" against other currencies on the local market and it was unlikely to be devalued in the near future. "There is a pressure from the country's exporters to devalue the taka," he said.
Sarker said the current inflation rate was 2.6 percent. "The lower inflation rate is because of lower foodgrain prices," he said.
